status: captured (home, product, science pages), judged by 2 combined AI jurors and the owner; interactions measured live

jury.note: 84.8k + 78.4k tokens for one site with three pages. The jurors read self-made contact sheets: the coordinator's inspector re-run had deleted the evidence sheets (rebuilt afterwards).

business.what: Prebiotic oatmeal (resistant starch, low-FODMAP, 8g fibre, 10g protein, 4 flavours), direct to consumer on Shopify, boxes of 6.
business.action_that_pays: Get Started → product page box builder. Captured during a 'Farewell Sale, 70% off everything': $9 a box instead of $30, minimum 4 boxes, all sales final.
business.source: captured home, product and science pages

claims.claim: The hero mixes a photo with vector brand elements, so it is not AI slop; the colour play differs from AI generators
claims.evidence: Food photograph in an arch frame with drawn leaves and oats breaking out of it (measured: leaf-1-front.png, leaf-1-back.png, leaf-2.png). They are raster cut-outs, not vectors, and the inspector counts them as photos (illustrations: 0), a measurement gap. Both jurors agree the hero is distinctive.

claims.claim: Scroll animation gives a different, not monotonous experience
claims.verdict: confirmed for variety, with two costs
claims.evidence: 2 full-screen sticky panels (hero photo grows to full width), section colours change, illustrations move. Costs: 6 endless marquees with no pause; 11-13 elements still move with reduced motion; 49 fps with 9-11 long frames under software rendering (relative only).

claims.claim: Looks simple, but colour and images make the message alive
claims.verdict: confirmed for mood, weaker for the message
claims.evidence: One flat colour field per section, 2 typefaces (Nib Pro 58% + Basis Grotesque 42%), 0 gradients, 0 shadows, CLS 0. The home page leaves out the facts that sell: no price, rating or fibre/protein numbers (all on the product page).

claims.claim: Hover states that change colour make the site feel alive
claims.verdict: partly: the useful ones signal that something opens
claims.evidence: Measured: 'Quite Nice can' rows turn italic and fill the arrow pill, then open a drawer; 'We're Picky' rows change background (lime/white) and open on click. The colour change is feedback; the meaning is in what opens. None of it exists on touch.

claims.claim: Flipping cards are common, but the interaction has a purpose the visitor sees
claims.verdict: purpose confirmed; mechanism corrected; fails on phones
claims.evidence: The cards do not flip: on hover the packet image is replaced by a photo of the finished bowl of that flavour (quitenice-cinnamon-hover.jpg). That answers 'what will I actually eat?'. Hover-only, so phone visitors never see the bowls; the 10 images without alt include these.

claims.claim: Overall neutral colour, minimalist, modern, friendly
claims.evidence: Few hues: 2 colour families (green, yellow) on cream, 5 values. But they are saturated full-bleed fields (forest green, mustard, lime), not neutral. Calm by hue count, bold by saturation.

interactions.what: Flavour card: packet → finished-bowl photo on hover
interactions.verdict: earns its place; needs a tap path

interactions.what: Benefit row → drawer with mechanism and journal citations
'We're Picky' row opens on click (colour change on hover)
interactions.purpose: what exactly is it free from?
interactions.verdict: click earns it; colour swap is feedback only

interactions.what: Hero photo grows from arch frame to full width on scroll
interactions.purpose: moves the eye from promise to food
interactions.verdict: earns its place (both jurors split: pacing vs mood)

interactions.purpose: none beyond repeating the 'We're Picky' list

interactions.what: Section background colour changes on scroll

library_candidates: Food photograph in an arch frame with drawn ingredients breaking out of it: product result and brand world in one first screen
Small drawn glyphs inside the headline sentence (oat, leaf, flower): memorable without an icon row
Benefit rows that open a drawer with the mechanism and citations: promise first, evidence on demand for a health claim
Packet-to-result swap on product cards: shows what the customer gets, not the package (with a tap path)
One flat colour field per story chapter from a small palette
Reassurance beside checkout: 'One-time purchase, nothing recurring', 'All sales final'
avoid: A home page with no price, rating or decision facts while the product page has them (4.85 from 54 reviews, $9)
Content that helps decide shown only on hover
Endless marquees with no pause; motion that ignores reduced motion
The product page loses the system: 17 font sizes, 12 colours, 6 display sizes with no scale, 32 small tap targets

owner_taste_signal: Visual 9 and ship 9: the owner values art direction (photo plus drawn brand elements, a custom serif, colour fields) and interactions that reveal meaning. The AI agrees on visual (distinctiveness 8, craft 7) and scores selling lower (business 5: no price or proof on the home page, a closing-down sale in a thin bar). The 2.4 gap is mostly business, not visual. Second 9 with a calm hue count (2 families), next to bold Maxima: the colour dial default 'bold' is one path, not the only one.
